chapter: Bill Robinson and Chuck and Chuckles
title: Galloping dominoes: dice decide the number of steps
summary: Green describes Robinson's game of galloping dominoes where the roll set the number of tap steps, aiming for eight, which fixed 32-bar choruses.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Well, he would say words, you know, a way of talking. He would introduce new plays, like in sports. Like who could throw the darts. You know. Who could balance the cards or make a card house, and so forth. Or who could play dice, dominoes, galloping dominoes. That was a pastime.
Well, it's some bones, square bones, and they've got numbers on them, like from one to six. And you

really can go up, and as a pair they would go from one to twelve -- two to twelve, like that. And you had to shake them in your hand like a fist, and then open your hand and they would roll out, and they would gallop and stop on some kind of number. And whatever number they'd stop on, the tap dancer would have to do that many steps. Tap steps. So he would always try to stop on eight, because that was equal to 24 bars of music, see. So if he'd make eight, that's his point, he has to make eight again. So eight would be 16. And that way, that's when they brought in the 32 bars of music, see. Because of his -- well, we called it sports. He was, like I say, a spirit. He was a great inspiration at that time to the people that was going along in the Depression. Things wasn't as rich as they were, but they was sending each other a thought.
It's interesting that you should mention the galloping dominoes, him playing with numbers, because you told me a very similar story about you and he playing pool on his 22nd birthday.
Why don't you tell me that story?
Well, that's it. I mean, he would introduce these plays which was known as a game. But I mean he made his living at it at the same time, by -- of course that was his job, was tap dancing, see, and --
